title: Coke vs Pepsi: Who Makes More Money? (2025 10-Ks)
text:
Coke vs Pepsi: Who Makes More Money? (2025 10-Ks)

# Coca-Cola vs PepsiCo: who makes more money?

PepsiCo is bigger: $93.9 billion in revenue against $47.9 billion for Coca-Cola, about 2.0 times as much. But Coca-Cola keeps more of each sale: $27.34 of every $100 versus $8.77. Across 5 rounds from their latest annual reports, Coca-Cola wins 4.

From each company's latest Form 10-K: Coca-Cola (year ended December 31, 2025) and PepsiCo (year ended December 27, 2025). Page updated November 9, 2026.

4 Coca-Cola

1 PepsiCo

### Revenue Money coming in

Coca-Cola $47.9 billion

PepsiCo Wins $93.9 billion

### Net profit After every cost and tax

Coca-Cola Wins $13.1 billion

PepsiCo $8.2 billion

### Kept per $100 of sales Profit margin

Coca-Cola Wins $27.34

PepsiCo $8.77

### Employees As each 10-K states it

Coca-Cola 65,900

PepsiCo More 306,000

### Revenue per employee Revenue ÷ employees

Coca-Cola Wins $727,481

PepsiCo $306,944

### Growth over 5 years Revenue, first to latest year shown

Coca-Cola Wins +45%

PepsiCo +33%

## How each one makes its money.

Coca-Cola

Coca-Cola mostly sells drink concentrate to bottlers, who mix, bottle and deliver it, and it also owns some bottlers itself.

Concentrate$28.5B 59% of total Finished drinks$19.5B 41% of total

PepsiCo

PepsiCo sells snacks (Lay's, Doritos, Quaker) and drinks (Pepsi, Gatorade), and makes more profit from snacks than from soda.

Drinks, North America$28.2B 30% of total

Snacks, North America$27.5B 29% of total

Europe, Middle East, Africa$18.0B 19% of total

Latin America$10.5B 11% of total

International drinks$5.0B 5% of total

## Quick answers.

### Who makes more money, Coca-Cola or PepsiCo?

PepsiCo: $93.9 billion in revenue against $47.9 billion.

### Which is more profitable, Coca-Cola or PepsiCo?

Coca-Cola keeps more of each dollar ($27.34 of every $100). In total profit, Coca-Cola made more: $13.1 billion.

### Which has more employees, Coca-Cola or PepsiCo?

PepsiCo, with about 306,000 against 65,900.

Sources: The Coca-Cola Company Form 10-K and PepsiCo, Inc. Form 10-K on SEC EDGAR. Fiscal years can end in different months, so each side uses its own latest year. Profit means net income.
